chapter: Town Hall, Vanguard and large works
title: The Town Hall concert fiasco and the ten-piece Vanguard band
summary: Mingus blames promoters for turning an open recording session into a concert; Max Gordon then offered him a band at the Village Vanguard.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Well, how -- what was the creative process in writing those pieces? Did you write them one at a time or did you have a suite in mind?

(Inaudible.) No, no, Town Hall was a not as far as my part was concerned. failure. As far as the promoters who put the concert on, they started rushing me to do it and make it a concert. It was supposed to have been an open recording session. Town Hall was supposed to have been where -- like I told them, I saw Duke Ellington when he first joined Columbia Records, in the theater, and they were recording. And they put all the equipment in this big theatre. And people found out about the recording session, so people came. Sat in the audience. I always wanted to do that to have an open recording session so people can see how a date goes down, how you play a section. And then stop, do it again. And that's (inaudible). George Wein William somehow got his money fucking face in it and made a concert out of it without letting me know. Because a lot of music I was playing could not be played as a concert, and when Columbia sections at we played the session (inaudible) a recording date. Plus I had copies of the stage and all that, just like Duke had his.
So everybody said it was a failure, so Max Gordon asked me to bring a big band into the Gate. He *(the Vanguard - ed.)

didn't say how big. So I decided on ten pieces, which I had (inaudible) written for when I was a kid. I forgot who all was in that. Oh, yeah, it was Four-Star Records. Baritone, for tenor, and an alto, trombone, two trumpets, no tuba. I added had a tuba here. I added had a tuba in New York, but originally there was no tuba.

And it was done specifically to show that Town Hall was not my fault. Because they put their tapes dates out with all the mistakes, because they let George William Wein edit it. What does George Williams know about editing my music?
